evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/page.tsx:145 — the flagship public listings SEARCH page destructures only `const { data, isLoading } = useListings(filters, currentPage);`. It never reads `isError`/`error`. On a failed query, TanStack Query returns data===undefined with isLoading===false, so the render at :337 does `listings={data?.data ?? []}` and passes it to ListingGrid with isLoading=false.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/ListingGrid.tsx:65-66 — with an empty array and isLoading=false, ListingGrid renders `<EmptyState icon="🔍" title={t('emptyTitle')} description={t('emptyDescription')} />`. Net effect: a backend/network failure on the most-trafficked public page is presented to the user as a benign "no properties found" empty state, with NO error message and NO retry affordance. Users (and crawlers) cannot distinguish 'API is down' from '0 matches'.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/query-provider.tsx:20-28 — the QueryClient sets only staleTime + refetchOnWindowFocus and does NOT set `throwOnError`/`useErrorBoundary`, so query errors are swallowed at the hook and are never surfaced to the app/[locale]/error.tsx error boundary either. There is thus no path by which this error becomes visible.

Confirmed inconsistency (not a stylistic nit): every SIBLING list page in the same segment DOES handle the error branch — price-map/page.tsx:45 (`isError`), realtor/listings/page.tsx:72 (`error`), inquiries/page.tsx:315 (`error`), agency/[slug]/page.tsx:28 (`isError`), agency/inquiries/page.tsx:87 (`error`), favorites/page.tsx:21 (`error`), saved-searches/page.tsx:300 (`error`). listings/page.tsx is the lone public search page that silently drops it. Landable frontend-only remedy: destructure `isError` from useListings and render an error state (with a retry/refetch) distinct from the empty state, matching the sibling pages. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck` + a Vitest/RTL test that makes useListings return isError and asserts an error UI (not EmptyState) renders. Confidence high: traced hook return -> page destructure -> ListingGrid empty-state fallback -> absent throwOnError, so the error is provably invisible in production.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/callback/page.tsx:146 — `

Completing login...

` is a hardcoded English literal shown to the user during the SSO callback wait. Every other user-facing string in the SAME component is already localized via next-intl: the component holds `const t = useTranslations('auth.callback')` (:80) and uses t('title'), t('invalidState'), t('returnHome'). This one visible string was missed.

reality-web is a public, SEO-indexed multi-locale portal. The messages catalogue ships 6 locales — messages/{sk,cs,en,de,hu,pl}.json — and the `auth.callback` block (en.json:107-111) currently defines only title/invalidState/returnHome, with no `loading`-style key, so a non-English visitor sees English mid-flow. (A generic `common.loading` = 'Loading...' exists at en.json:118 but is unused here and semantically weaker.) Landable frontend-only remedy: add e.g. `auth.callback.completing` ("Completing login…") to all 6 messages/*.json and replace the literal with `t('completing')`. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck` + the repo's i18n key-parity check. Confidence high on the gap (literal is right there and t() is already in scope); severity low — cosmetic, non-blocking, no functional/security impact.
